title: A Systematic Literature Review of AI Readiness in the Public Sector: A Conceptual Distinction Between BI Systems, Analytics and AI
content: Governments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to automate public services, yet many public entities lack a clear way to assess how ready they are to adopt it. This study presents a systematic literature review of AI readiness in the public sector and clarifies the conceptual distinction between business intelligence (BI), analytics and AI. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 173 records published between 2015 and 2026 were retrieved from IEEE Xplore, ProQuest, Emerald Insight and Taylor & Francis, and 65 studies were retained for thematic synthesis. A supplementary search of Scopus and Web of Science returned 70 records, including 33 of the included studies, and identified no additional eligible studies. Of the 65 studies, 56 (86.2%) are indexed in Scopus and 29 (44.6%) in Web of Science. Four themes emerged: AI readiness as a multidimensional construct; governance and institutional influence; human, behavioural and organisational factors; and KPI-driven measurement supported by BI. The review shows that BI, analytics and AI form successive layers, moving from reporting what happened to predicting outcomes and automating decisions, with each layer raising the data, skills and governance requirements of an organisation. Building on this synthesis, a socio-technical AI readiness assessment framework is proposed that groups readiness factors into four domains and operationalises them through BI-enabled KPIs. Only two of the included studies address Jordan, which highlights the need for context-specific readiness assessment in developing countries.
